name: asOneFormula
title: Combine Formulas of a Set of Objects

origin.description: The names of all variables used in the formulas extracted from the objects defined in ... are converted into a single linear formula, with the variables names separated by +.

arguments.text: objects, or lists of objects, from which a formula can be extracted.

arguments.name: omit
arguments.text: an optional character vector with the names of variables to be omitted from the returned formula. Defaults to c(".", "pi").

origin.value: a one-sided linear formula with all variables named in the formulas extracted from the objects in ..., except the ones listed in omit.
origin.example:
.libPaths(c(path.expand("~/R/library"), .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(nlme))
asOneFormula(y ~ x + z | g, list(~ w, ~ t * sin(2 * pi)))

translation.description: Collect every variable name appearing in the given formulas (including nested lists) into one one-sided linear formula, joined with +.

arguments.name: *objects
arguments.text: Formula strings, or lists of formula strings, in the same shapes R accepts for ....

arguments.name: omit
arguments.text: Variable names to drop. The default is (".", "pi"), matching R.

translation.details: Function names in calls are excluded from the variable list, following R's all.vars. The result formats like deparse(asOneFormula(...)) in R. An empty variable set returns ~1.
translation.value: A Formula object whose str() is the one-sided formula text.
translation.example:
from nlme.asoneformula import asOneFormula

print(asOneFormula("y ~ x + z | g", ["~ w", "~ t * sin(2 * pi)"]))
